VERIFIED BY EXECUTION. I built a crossnobis plan from the ?plan_crossnobis example and tried both verbs:

  class(plan)                       effect_crossnobis_plan
  rdm(plan)                         ERROR: RDM requires a geometry plan or complete effect form.
  rsa(plan, models = list(m = ...)) ERROR: RSA requires a geometry plan or complete effect form.

So the recommendation is real and unimplemented, confirmed against the running package rather than from a reviewer report. The gate is R/views.R:104-108, which I also read directly - it admits only the geometry-plan branch above it and anything inheriting effect_form, and rejects everything else.

A SHARPER PROBLEM SURFACED BY THE TEST, which belongs on bd-01KZY9B80RMYJD4QDAFS5ZBQSM as well. The message a user actually receives is:

  RDM requires a geometry plan or complete effect form.

A user holding an object of class effect_crossnobis_plan - which they built by calling a function named plan_crossnobis - is told that RDM requires a plan. They HAVE a plan. The message names a category the object appears to belong to and refuses it anyway, with no indication that a different KIND of plan is meant, and no mention of crossnobis() as the verb that does accept it.

That makes this worse than a missing feature. A user who reasonably expects the RDM verb to work on a crossnobis plan gets a message that reads as a contradiction, and the natural next inference is that they built the plan wrong rather than that they used the wrong verb.

MINIMUM FIX EVEN IF THE FEATURE IS NOT BUILT: the message should name the object it received and the verb that accepts it -

  RDM requires a geometry plan or complete effect form; you supplied an
  <effect_crossnobis_plan>. Use crossnobis(plan, ...) for crossnobis estimates,
  or plan_geometry() to build a geometry plan.

That is a message-only change, independent of whether the branch is ever added.
